title: Scalar-restricted K-injectives are acyclic for pro-etale direct image
statement: On the original pro-etale sites of schemes X and Y, let f:X→Y, let B→C be a map of sheaves of commutative rings on X, and let D→f_*B be any structural map of ring sheaves. Rings and modules lie in the independent universe max u (t+1), as in [def-pur-completed-pushforward-models]. For any supplied RightImage model F of the additive pushforward of B-modules to D-modules and any K-injective C-module cochain complex I, the universal derived unit of F at the scalar restriction of I to B is an isomorphism. The rings B and C may be presented as RingCat-valued sheaves with sectionwise commutativity. Neither flatness of B→C nor commutativity of D is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied to scalar restriction; Tag 08FI, restriction of K-injectives to a localized site; Tag 0A95, sectionwise detection.

proof.text: Lift the sectionwise commutative ring sheaves and their map to CommRingCat. Resolve the scalar-restricted complex by a quasi-isomorphism j to a K-injective B-module complex K, using Grothendieck abelianness and K-injective resolutions in the independent coefficient universe.

For each object U of the original pro-etale site, restrict I, K and j to X/U. Exact slice restriction preserves the quasi-isomorphism, and preserves K-injectivity of I and K. Apply scalar-restriction acyclicity for sections to these two complexes and j.

Global sections on X/U identify naturally with evaluation at its terminal object. The resulting quasi-isomorphism is sections of j over U. Direct image evaluates j on the base-changed target objects, so sectionwise detection makes f_*(j) a quasi-isomorphism of module complexes.

The supplied derived unit is invertible at K. Its naturality square for j has the other two sides Q(f_*(j)) and F(Q(j)) invertible. Two-out-of-three for isomorphisms therefore makes its unit at the scalar restriction of I invertible.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0D6E, 08FI and 0A95; proof on the original site by evaluating a restricted K-injective resolution on every slice.

lean.statement:
theorem restrictionPushforward_acyclic {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {B C : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}}
    {D : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}}
    (hB : ∀ (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (a b : B.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    (hC : ∀ (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (a b : C.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    (a : B ⟶ C) (c : D ⟶ (ringPush.{t, u} f).obj B)
    [(push f c).Additive] (F : RightImage (push f c))
    (I : CochainComplex (Mod X C) ℤ) (hI : I.IsKInjective) :
    IsIso (F.unit.app
      (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u (t + 1)} a).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj I))
